purpose: A development companion for coding agents working with TYPO3, for three audiences: the core contributor, the extension author and the site developer. It establishes the project and installation the agent works in, supplies current, version-bound TYPO3 knowledge, and hands task workflows to the skills that own them. A scope answer describes what is present and does not treat it as correct. The server also answers what is registered in the installation it was started in. Where that installation does not boot or does not exist, the bundled knowledge and the installed packages answer, and the answer says which. Every answer says which TYPO3 versions it holds for and which kind of work it belongs to.

instructions.start: Start every task with typo3_project_describe. It answers the TYPO3 version, the project's own extensions, its sites, and the commands the repository declares. A check you recommend that the repository does not declare is a wrong answer however sensible it sounds. Then call typo3_task_guide for the workflow the task belongs to. Call it again at the first test, check, commit or shipped file the task did not name. Not every task ends in a patch. It also answers a triage of the backlog, whether a report still reproduces, and what a fix costs. What changed, which branch you are on, whether a path still exists, and how the core implements something are yours to read in the checkout.

index.question: backend markup or a CSS class
a label, added or reworded
index.call: typo3_label_lookup with the XLF resource the code at hand uses; a match elsewhere is not reusable

index.question: what a version broke, deprecated or added, on a major you have not built on lately
the commit message, yours as much as the core's, and its branches
the whole procedure, not one fact out of it
index.call: typo3_rule_lookup with a documentId typo3_project_describe lists

instructions.note: Activate the typo3-* skill that covers the task: it makes these calls.
instructions.then:
targetVersion or the version the server read filters the answers, and a statement that does not hold on every covered line carries its range.

Query this server in English whatever language you speak with the user. Its match is lexical, so a query in another language reaches only the loanwords. Translate the subject before you call, and the answer back.

typo3_server_scope says what it covers, by which tool, and which installation it reads.

outside.start: This server started outside any repository, so it reads no project and no installation. Pass targetVersion on every call: the version the user named, or ask, or say in the answer which one you assumed. Where the answer depends on the user's project, tell them that TYPO3_DEV_COMPANION_ROOT in this server's entry lets it read that project. Call typo3_task_guide for the workflow the task belongs to. Call it again at the first test, check, commit or shipped file the task did not name. Not every task ends in a patch. It also answers a triage of the backlog, whether a report still reproduces, and what a fix costs.

calls.the whole procedure, not one fact out of: typo3_rule_lookup by topic, then by the documentId a match names

outside.note: The typo3://skill resources are the task workflows; read the one that covers the task: it makes these calls.

covers.topic: Contribution rules and review readiness
covers.depth: Curated prose. The rules a patch is judged by, not a full style guide.

covers.topic: Gerrit workflow: setup, pushing, amending, opening a patch set on somebody else's change, backports
covers.depth: Curated prose, command level. Covers the local git side; it cannot talk to the Gerrit server.

covers.topic: The JavaScript and CSS the core commits beside the sources they are built from
covers.depth: Curated prose, command level: which source tree builds which committed file, how a minified file is diffed, and a rebuild in a separate worktree. It covers a backport that conflicts in a built file. typo3_test_run_guide names the suite per branch.

covers.topic: What a patch loses when the code moved under it, which no conflict reports
covers.depth: Four checks against a checkout: what main changed on the paths since the base, whether a fix in a rewritten file survives, which removed members still have callers, and which suites cover the rewritten paths. Plus the git call that shows stale committed JavaScript.

covers.topic: Forge issues: what one says and what was decided about it, which other issues describe the same thing, and what stands open in the core's backlog
covers.depth: The tracker's API, read live. By number: the report, the comments that decided it, related issues, files and review changes. By words: unranked text matches. As a backlog: the core's issues by age, neglect or recency, with filters and a breakdown. Each says whether the installed packages still ship the cited code.

covers.topic: Gerrit changes: whether a patch already exists, what state its review is in, which changes touch a path or name a wording, and what stands open in the core's review backlog
covers.depth: The anonymous Gerrit REST API, read live. By change number, Change-Id or commit: the change, its siblings, patch set, paths, votes, comments, chain and trailers, and on request the review log and the CI jobs that failed. By words and path: the matching changes. As a backlog: open changes by age or neglect, with filters. A private change is invisible.

covers.topic: Commit messages
covers.depth: Rules plus a working draft and a check, including 72-character body wrapping. workflow="project" serves the same conventions for a repository without Forge issues or release branches. The user-invoked prompt commit_message exposes the same guide.

covers.topic: How the comments and docblocks a patch carries have to read
covers.depth: Ten rules, each with a rejected sentence and its replacement: say what is, name who acts, one thought per sentence, and seven more. Whether a comment is owed at all is the codebase's own rule.

covers.topic: The changelog entry a core patch owes: which type, which directory a backport goes into, and what checks the file
covers.depth: Curated prose, with the skeleton in the documentation-changelog hint: which of the four types a change owes, and which release directory the file goes in, keyed on the branches the patch reaches. It names the core's template and the command that writes the file.

covers.topic: What a new core issue carries: the fields of a Bug, where the area comes from, who sets the target version, and the markup the description renders as
covers.depth: Curated prose for writing a report: the trackers, the fields of a Bug, the order a report is written in, and the Textile markup the description renders as. typo3_issue_report_guide drafts and checks the issue and opens the filled-in form. Filing it needs an account and stays the caller's.

covers.topic: Core testing suites: runTests.sh options and targeted invocation
covers.depth: Every suite this knowledge base knows, with the command, the targeted form, and when to use it. For a path outside the core, the answer states the boundary instead of a command.

covers.topic: Proving what a rendering contains, where a finding turns on it and no test in the checkout produces it
covers.depth: The throwaway functional test that renders one page and prints the result: the cObj, how output leaves the test, one marker per region, the targeted invocation, and where the RTE setup comes from per version. It does not say what parseFunc does to a snippet.

covers.topic: Exercising the system resource publisher from a functional test
covers.depth: Which file system publisher a test instance runs and why, why publishing does nothing for a package below the public path, and which state at the target fails for real. From TYPO3 14.

covers.topic: Timing a code path between a patch and its parent, where a review asks what a change costs at runtime
covers.depth: The throwaway functional test that times one path on the patch and on its parent, so the finding is a ratio, and what the number leaves out.

covers.topic: The PHPUnit configuration an extension runs its own tests with
covers.depth: The two Build/ files, whole, one variant per PHPUnit the paired typo3/testing-framework release allows, with the attributes a copy must correct and the environment a functional run reads. It names no dependency constraint.

covers.topic: What an extension's Documentation/ directory consists of
covers.depth: The files that make a directory a manual: a minimal guides.xml, the Index.rst header and toctree, two look-alikes that are no template, and the render command with the flag that fails on a broken directive. It does not write the chapters.

covers.topic: Whether an API is there on a TYPO3 major the package declares and the installation does not have
covers.depth: How to settle it without a run: which declaration matters, what the changelog settles, and how to read one symbol off the other branch. It states no signature, because a bundled one goes wrong at the next release.

covers.topic: What the backend styleguide states about a component, and what it leaves unstated
covers.depth: Where the styleguide lives per major, what its listing settles, and the two ways a demo is misread: an example does not mark its required parts, and the classes in its template are not the whole component.

covers.topic: Which route a package's own CSS or JavaScript takes into a page, and what proves it still carries
covers.depth: Every route a package's CSS or JavaScript takes into a page, with its check: the backend import map, PageRenderer calls, TypoScript includeCSS, the AssetCollector, and the later ViewHelpers. It ends with what to do after a rebuild renamed or dropped a file.

covers.topic: Running a package's own suite against a TYPO3 major it declares and the installation does not have
covers.depth: The procedure: what CI already covers, a second Composer root resolved for the other major, what that root resolves differently, and which checks are worth a run there. It installs nothing itself.

covers.topic: The Playwright suite a project runs its browser tests from
covers.depth: The configuration, the backend login per TYPO3 major, and one spec, whole. Beside them: where the base URL and the credentials come from, and which locator on the login form is ambiguous. It installs nothing.

covers.topic: Booting a cloned project repository into a running installation
covers.depth: The steps from a clone to a site that answers: what the clone lacks, why the environment starts twice, where the data comes from, and what a login costs. It runs nothing.

covers.topic: Renaming an extension key, its tables or its CTypes in an installation that holds records
covers.depth: What a rename touches on the data side, in order: new tables and nothing dropped, the positional INSERT ... SELECT trap, and every column that stores a name as a value. It runs nothing, and the proof is a query.

covers.topic: Looking at a change in a real browser, against the installation that has the content
covers.depth: Which installation can show the case, how a browser in a container reaches a DDEV site, and where a harness and its screenshots go so neither reaches a commit. It runs nothing.

covers.topic: Drawing the icon a content element is picked by, and the set it belongs to
covers.depth: The 16-pixel box of the core's content icons, what the set varies to tell elements apart, and the check that a set works at rendered size. Whether an identifier resolves is typo3_icon_lookup's question.

covers.topic: Proving that a TypoScript condition matched against a running installation
covers.depth: How a condition's verdict is read off the page: a marker only the guarded branch renders, the negative control, and the cache between two runs. It requests nothing and flushes nothing.

covers.topic: Proving that a change to how a site renders changed only what it meant to
covers.depth: How the pages to capture are chosen from the content that exists, why the baseline is captured twice, which cache keeps the old compiled Fluid, and how the diffs are read. It requests nothing and flushes nothing.

covers.topic: Reporting a security defect in TYPO3: who receives it, what the report carries, and what is not done with it in the meantime
covers.depth: TYPO3's published policy, from SECURITY.md and the security team's pages, for the core and for extensions alike. It rates no finding.

covers.topic: Where the upstream contribution documentation is
covers.depth: The official contribution guide is not bundled. This names its entry points, so a question past the local documents goes to the source.

covers.topic: Core conventions: DI, events and hooks, TCA and FormEngine, FormEngine data providers, DataHandler, routing, Fluid templates and ViewHelpers, frontend page rendering with PAGEVIEW, how a sitepackage is laid out, records in the frontend and the routing for them, registering a content element, Extbase plugins, TypoScript site sets and TSconfig, language files, upgrade wizards, frontend DataProcessors, upgrading an installation, testing strategy, assembling a test suite for a project extension, setting up static analysis and the coding standards fixer for an extension, browser and accessibility tests with Playwright
covers.depth: Conventions per subsystem, matched by path or topic, from both angles: what a change to the subsystem has to satisfy, and how the mechanism is used. It describes how the core is built, never what your checkout contains.

covers.topic: Task workflows for extension, sitepackage and project work: backend modules, content elements, package health, change review, distribution content, asset builds, sitepackages, documentation, tests, the development installation, and upgrades
covers.depth: The skills this server publishes, one resource per workflow: the order of the steps, with the lookup that owns each fact. bin/typo3-dev-companion install writes the same files into the client's own skills directory.

covers.topic: The core's own task workflows: saying what an open issue still claims, getting a patch under review into a checkout, writing a patch and carrying it to review, and reviewing somebody else's patch set
covers.depth: The same shape, with steps that stop at the core repository: the Forge issue, the patch set ref, runTests.sh, the changelog entry and the Gerrit push. A triage writes a verdict only, and a checkout stops at conflicts the patch does not decide.

covers.topic: Official TYPO3 API, reference and tutorial documentation
covers.depth: Live search in the tables of contents of TYPO3 Explained, TypoScript Explained, the TCA Reference and the ViewHelper Reference, for one covered release. Pass a result URL back to read the page as text. An unreachable service is not an empty search.

covers.topic: Whether a documentation permalink resolves, what it lands on, and which identifier replaces an old docs.typo3.org URL
covers.depth: The Sphinx inventory of each manual. Per identifier: the page and anchor, the registered type, and the other spellings. Per URL: the identifiers that point at it, or candidates where the page is gone. Many at a time. It says which branch answered. An extension manual outside the core is not answered.

covers.topic: Backend CSS architecture, design tokens, class naming
covers.depth: Curated prose covering the Sass sources, the token contract, and the component structure.

covers.topic: Backend UI components: markup, variants, custom properties
covers.depth: A curated subset, not every core CSS class. The active installation supplies presence, classes, custom properties and styleguide markup. A version-bound snapshot is the fallback.
covers.source: installed EXT:backend and EXT:styleguide files; knowledge/catalog/component/entries.json as index and fallback — read from the installation being worked in, not from a bundled snapshot.

covers.topic: Which extensions the TYPO3 core ships, and on which versions
covers.depth: Every system extension of every covered line, by key and package name, with its purpose and version range. It answers for an extension that is not installed. A miss means not a system extension there.

covers.topic: Where the core keeps its own worked examples
covers.depth: An index of the core's worked examples: one line per directory, its package and its versions. Use it where a hint is thin.

covers.topic: Translation domains: how the domain of an XLF file is derived
covers.depth: Computed, not a snapshot: the core's path-to-domain rules, ported, so any XLF path resolves, a new one included. Where the installation predates translation domains, the answer is the full LLL:EXT: reference.

covers.topic: How current the catalogs are
covers.depth: Whether component contracts came from the active installation or the bundled fallback, plus the core revision, branch, and verification date behind that fallback.

covers.topic: What the installation you are working in supplies: backend component contracts, labels, icons, backend modules, Fluid namespaces, effective configuration, the columns TYPO3 derives for a table beside what its database has, the services its container assembles, and the data structure one of its flex fields resolves to
covers.depth: Answered by that installation, across its active packages, project extensions included. Its console answers where a command exists. Where none does, or where the command carries less, TYPO3 boots in a subprocess and its container answers. Package files answer where neither works. Label reuse is limited to the XLF resource of the consuming code. Every answer names its source.
covers.source: the discovered TYPO3 installation — read from the installation being worked in, not from a bundled snapshot.

covers.topic: What is in a table of one of this project's own extensions
covers.depth: The rows and their counts: per page, live, hidden or deleted, with uid, label, timestamps and flags, narrowed by exact values. Only the tables of this project's own extensions are read. Every answer says it used the shell user's database access, not a backend user's permissions.
covers.source: the discovered installation, booted, with one grouped count and one row read against its database. What a row carries is fixed here rather than composed by the caller.

covers.topic: The project around the installation: its extensions, its sites and their sets, its own commands, the environment it declares and what that environment runs by itself, and what one of those extensions registers
covers.depth: Read from the repository's files — composer.json, package.json, config/sites, .github/workflows and .ddev — so it answers on a fresh clone. It states the declared commands, the PHP and Node versions each place declares, and the DDEV hooks and pull recipes. Per extension: its tables, content elements, modules, icons, site sets, services, middlewares and Fluid namespaces. It describes and does not rate.
covers.source: the discovered project — read from the installation being worked in, not from a bundled snapshot.

covers.topic: What a TYPO3 version broke, deprecated, added or noted
covers.depth: One entry per change, searched by words, type and version, from the changelog docs.typo3.org renders after every merge. The core package on disk answers what docs.typo3.org does not list. Each entry names its source.
covers.source: docs.typo3.org for every covered major, and the discovered installation for what docs.typo3.org does not list or where it does not answer. Not a bundled snapshot either way.

covers.topic: Which published extensions cover a subject, and which versions of one the TYPO3 Extension Repository has published
covers.depth: The registry's API, read live by key: every published version with its state, upload day, declared TYPO3 majors and constraint, and whether a named version is already taken. A query searches the TER and Packagist by subject. It reads nothing inside a package.

doesNotCover.topic: Your git state: changed files, branch, working tree, commit message, history
doesNotCover.why: This server reads the directory it was started in, but it never runs git. It does not know what you changed, what you committed, or which branch you are on.
doesNotCover.instead: Ask git. "git show --name-only --format=%B HEAD" gives the changed paths for typo3_test_run_guide and the message for typo3_commit_message_guide.

doesNotCover.topic: PHP source as code: where the core implements a behaviour, a method signature, whether a class or member is @internal or public API, an implementation to copy
doesNotCover.why: No core sources ship here. Package files are read for what they register, never for a signature or an annotation. So whether a removed method was public API is a question for the checkout.
doesNotCover.instead: Read the class in the checkout or below vendor/. typo3_backend_module_lookup gives the route identifiers a registry composed, typo3_schema_lookup the assembled TCA, typo3_changelog_lookup what a version changed, and typo3_hint_lookup what a subsystem is built to.

doesNotCover.topic: Which test covers a given file
doesNotCover.why: Test coverage is a property of the checkout, and no index of it is bundled.
doesNotCover.instead: Core tests mirror the class path below typo3/sysext/<ext>/Tests/Unit/ and Tests/Functional/, so typo3/sysext/core/Classes/DataHandling/DataHandler.php is covered by typo3/sysext/core/Tests/Unit/DataHandling/DataHandlerTest.php. Look the file up there, then ask typo3_test_run_guide for the targeted runTests.sh invocation.

doesNotCover.topic: Frontend theming: the CSS and the JavaScript a website renders
doesNotCover.why: Everything here about CSS and TypeScript describes the backend interface: its Sass, its --typo3-* tokens and its color schemes. For a theme, those are the wrong answer. How a theme extension is laid out is covered in the hints.
doesNotCover.instead: typo3_hint_lookup withholds the backend CSS and TypeScript hints where a task names the frontend. The styling itself is documented at https://docs.typo3.org.

doesNotCover.topic: Whether an uncatalogued component or CSS class exists on your branch
doesNotCover.why: The searchable index is a curated subset, not every class in backend.css. Without an installation, the curated entries fall back to one pinned core snapshot.
doesNotCover.instead: The component answer names its source and the snapshot revision. Inspect the installed backend CSS or the target checkout for a class outside the index.

doesNotCover.topic: Gerrit beyond what an anonymous read answers: the hunks of a patch set, a draft comment nobody published, what CI did beyond the line its bot posted, and anything a private change carries
doesNotCover.why: The review API is read without a credential, so drafts and private changes are out of reach. The hunks are read in the checkout, not over the API. Nothing here writes to Gerrit.
doesNotCover.instead: typo3_gerrit_lookup answers the change, its patch set, paths, votes, comments and fetch ref. Voting, commenting and uploading stay yours, and typo3://guides/core/contribution/gerrit-workflow covers them.

doesNotCover.topic: What someone else's extension does: the API, the options and the documentation of a package the core does not ship
doesNotCover.why: Writing an extension is covered. The inside of somebody else's package is not: its API, its releases and its documentation. Its published TER record is answered, and typo3_system_extension_lookup says whether a name belongs to the core.
doesNotCover.instead: Read that extension's documentation. typo3_extension_describe answers what an installed extension registers, and typo3_ter_lookup what is published under its key.

doesNotCover.topic: Deciding one site's configuration: its languages, its base and the variants per environment, its error handling, and the steps that install it
doesNotCover.why: A site set is a convention and is covered. What one installation writes into config/sites/<identifier>/config.yaml is that site's decision. typo3_project_describe reads the file and does not compose it.
doesNotCover.instead: Read what the project has with typo3_project_describe, ask typo3_hint_lookup with id=site-sets how a set resolves, and take the format from https://docs.typo3.org/.

doesNotCover.topic: Running an installation: server and container setup, deployment, backups, the editorial use of the backend
doesNotCover.why: The knowledge base covers what is written into a TYPO3 project. Operating the installation around it is a different subject. A project's own environment file is the exception.
doesNotCover.instead: Use https://docs.typo3.org/. typo3_project_describe reports what the environment file configures, and typo3_hint_lookup with id=php-versions says which interpreter to declare.

doesNotCover.topic: The content of the installation's own tables: a record of pages, tt_content, a file reference, a workspace, a user
doesNotCover.why: The content model is answered, and the content is read, never written. typo3_record_lookup reads rows with the shell user's database access rather than a backend user's permissions, and every answer says so.
doesNotCover.instead: Write records in the backend or with vendor/bin/typo3. Ask typo3_schema_lookup for a table's columns, typo3_record_lookup for its rows, typo3_flexform_lookup for a flex column, and typo3_hint_lookup for what DataHandler expects.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: Which files the task actually touches
checkoutDiscovery.how: git status --short and git diff --name-only in the core checkout, then call typo3_hint_lookup with those paths for the conventions that apply to them.
Core tests mirror the class path below typo3/sysext/<ext>/Tests/Unit/ and Tests/Functional/. Find the file there, then ask typo3_test_run_guide for the targeted runTests.sh invocation.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: The branch you are on and the branches the change is meant for
checkoutDiscovery.how: git branch --show-current. In the normal case the patch targets main and the merging core team member handles the backport; push to a release branch only when the bug does not exist on main.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: Whether the paths, classes, labels, and identifiers named in an answer still exist on that branch
checkoutDiscovery.how: Call typo3_component_lookup for curated backend components: it reads the active installation when the target matches. For uncatalogued code or another target branch, grep the checkout; typo3_snapshot_scope names the fallback revision.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: Whether an icon identifier is registered, and which one spells the shape you want
checkoutDiscovery.how: Ask typo3_icon_lookup: it reads the registry of the installation this server was started in, the T3Icons set and every installed package included. Where there is no reachable installation, the same three places can be read by hand — typo3/sysext/core/Resources/Public/Icons/T3Icons/icons.json, the Configuration/Icons.php of each package, and typo3/sysext/core/Resources/Public/Icons/Flags/ for the flags-* family.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: Whether a label for this wording already exists
checkoutDiscovery.how: Identify the XLF resource already used at the consuming code, then ask typo3_label_lookup with that resource. It applies the installation's resource overrides, but a match from another module or package is not reusable in this context. Where the console cannot be reached it reads the installed package's XLF file instead and says so; only where there is no installation at all is there nothing to ask.

routing.when: Asked to review, audit or assess a project, a site package or an extension, before the first file
routing.call: typo3_project_describe, then typo3_task_guide for the workflow and typo3_extension_describe for each extension in scope

routing.when: Going through the core's open issues — the oldest, the ones nobody has touched for years, or what stands open in one area such as the RTE or the backend UI
routing.call: typo3_forge_lookup with backlog="oldest" or "stale", narrowed with category in the user's own words and with tracker, then typo3_forge_lookup with the number of the one being taken further

routing.when: What one person has filed on the tracker, or what they still hold — one contributor's backlog, or what a core team member has open
routing.call: typo3_forge_lookup with backlog="oldest" and involving, or reportedBy or assignedTo for one side, and status="all" for the years. Never query by the name, which matches the text of an issue.

routing.when: Writing a core bug report or filling in the new-issue form on forge.typo3.org, including the issue a patch's Resolves: trailer names
routing.call: typo3_issue_report_guide, which drafts, checks for duplicates and fills in the form; typo3_rule_lookup with documentId="core/contribution/reporting-an-issue" for the reasons

routing.when: Taking a Forge issue on, before believing what it describes
routing.call: typo3_forge_lookup for the issue and its comments, again with query in its own words for duplicates, then typo3_gerrit_lookup with the number for an existing patch

routing.when: Before writing a patch for a file, or asking whether a fix was attempted before
routing.call: typo3_gerrit_lookup with path, and open for the changes under review, then with query in the words of a commit message

routing.when: Starting a review session without a change in hand: the oldest, the small, the nearly voted, mine, or the ones I voted on
routing.call: typo3_gerrit_lookup with backlog "oldest" or "stale" and its filters, then with change for the one picked

routing.when: Asking which branches carry the fix a commit hash names
routing.call: typo3_gerrit_lookup with commit: the change, its backports by Change-Id, and the branches each Releases: trailer claims

routing.when: Reviewing a TYPO3 core patch rather than a project or an extension
routing.call: typo3_gerrit_lookup for the change, typo3_rule_lookup per obligation, typo3_changelog_lookup for precedent, typo3_test_run_guide with the paths, then typo3_commit_message_guide with workflow="core"

routing.when: Settling a finding on what a rendering contains rather than on a diff: TypoScript defaults, lib.parseFunc, or a PHP change to the request pipeline, an error handler or a page renderer caller
routing.call: typo3_rule_lookup with documentId="core/testing/proving-a-rendering"

routing.when: Settling a finding on what a change costs at runtime
routing.call: typo3_rule_lookup with documentId="core/testing/timing-a-code-path"

routing.when: Writing a core patch: taking a Forge issue on, fixing a core bug, deprecating or removing core API, or amending a patch after review
routing.call: typo3_task_guide with the paths you are changing, then typo3_hint_lookup with the same ones, typo3_test_run_guide for the suites that can fail, and typo3_rule_lookup for the Gerrit workflow

routing.when: Starting a core task and looking for the applicable conventions and checks
routing.call: typo3_task_guide

routing.when: About to invent a layout, a directory structure or a test harness — the core has probably worked one out already
routing.call: typo3_reference_list

routing.when: About to write backend markup or invent a CSS class name, layout classes included. A miss means uncurated, not outside the subject.
routing.call: typo3_component_lookup

routing.when: About to run tests or any other core check
routing.call: typo3_test_run_guide

routing.when: Getting Build/Scripts/runTests.sh to run in this checkout: a suite that fails before it reads a file, a fresh clone, a worktree, or the pre-commit hook
routing.call: typo3_script_lookup with the task in your own words

routing.when: Working in a concrete file and unsure about the subsystem's conventions
routing.call: typo3_hint_lookup

routing.when: Debugging, where there is no subject yet — something renders, saves or builds wrong and which subsystem does it is the question
routing.call: typo3_hint_lookup with task written as the symptom, in the words the failure showed in

routing.when: Needing the official API, reference or tutorial documentation for a covered TYPO3 version
routing.call: typo3_documentation_lookup with several short English queries and targetVersion, then with page and the same targetVersion to read a selected result

routing.when: Writing or checking a documentation link, or replacing a docs.typo3.org URL with a permalink
routing.call: typo3_permalink_lookup with identifiers or urls, many at a time

routing.when: Writing or amending the commit message
routing.call: typo3_commit_message_guide, whose default is a repository of your own

routing.when: Pushing for review, amending a patch set — your own or another author's — or backporting
routing.call: typo3_rule_lookup with a Gerrit query

routing.when: A catalog lookup found nothing that should exist
routing.call: typo3_snapshot_scope, then typo3_feedback_record

routing.when: Needing the translation domain an XLF file resolves to
routing.call: typo3_translation_domain_lookup with the path

routing.when: About to write user-facing text or invent a label key
routing.call: typo3_label_lookup with words from the wording and the XLF resource used at the consuming code

routing.when: About to reference a backend icon identifier: TCA, a module, a wizard, a backend template
routing.call: typo3_icon_lookup

routing.when: Needing a configuration value as it really is at runtime, not as the core ships it
routing.call: typo3_configuration_lookup with the TYPO3_CONF_VARS path as configurationPath

routing.when: Working on a backend module and needing its registration, its sub-routes, or whether the page tree navigates it
routing.call: typo3_backend_module_lookup

routing.when: Unsure which Fluid namespace prefixes a template may use undeclared
routing.call: typo3_fluid_namespace_list

routing.when: Needing which arguments a Fluid ViewHelper registers, with the type, the default and whether it takes arbitrary ones beyond them
routing.call: typo3_documentation_lookup with the tag name such as f:asset.css and the targetVersion

routing.when: About to recommend a command, or asking what this project consists of
routing.call: typo3_project_describe

routing.when: Starting work on a TYPO3 major you have not built on recently, or planning an upgrade to one this installation does not have — before asking what a version changed
routing.call: typo3_changelog_lookup

routing.when: Asking whether a pattern still works in a version; the silence of the changelog is no answer
routing.call: typo3_documentation_lookup with targetVersion and short English queries, then with page

routing.when: Writing against a core API in a package that declares a TYPO3 major the installation does not have
routing.call: typo3_project_describe, then typo3_rule_lookup with documentId="extension/compatibility/a-declared-major-that-is-not-installed"

routing.when: Sweeping deprecations in a package that declares more than one TYPO3 major
routing.call: typo3_changelog_lookup with the issue number of the deprecation, for the sibling entries and their versions

routing.when: About to claim that a change holds on a declared major the installation does not have
routing.call: typo3_rule_lookup with documentId="extension/compatibility/running-on-a-declared-major-that-is-not-installed"

routing.when: Upgrading or maintaining an installation, and needing the order of operations
routing.call: typo3_task_guide, then typo3_project_describe and typo3_changelog_lookup for what this one is and what the target version changed

routing.when: Auditing or preparing an extension release, before calling a version unreleased
routing.call: typo3_ter_lookup with the extension key and version, then typo3_hint_lookup with id="extension-ter-release"

routing.when: About to build a feature, before the first file: a published extension may already do it
routing.call: typo3_ter_lookup with query for the subject, then typo3_hint_lookup with id="extension-reuse" to weigh the best match against your own build

routing.when: Working in one extension and needing what it registers
routing.call: typo3_extension_describe with its key

routing.when: About to claim that an extension is (or is not) part of the core, or to require one
routing.call: typo3_system_extension_lookup

routing.when: About to write or review an ext_tables.sql, and needing to know which columns TYPO3 creates by itself
routing.call: typo3_schema_lookup with the table

routing.when: Writing or reading a FlexForm. The file the registration names is not what the backend resolves.
routing.call: typo3_flexform_lookup with the table, the flex column and the record values that decide the structure, CType for a content element

routing.when: Asking which class stands behind an interface here, whether a service is public, what a constructor is handed, or what registers into an extension point
routing.call: typo3_service_lookup with a substring of the id or the class, or with one exact tag

routing.when: Asking whether the database matches what the extensions and the TCA declare
routing.call: typo3_schema_lookup with the table

routing.when: Asking what is actually stored in one of this project's own tables, or how much of it there is
routing.call: typo3_record_lookup with the table, and columns, groupBy, count or where as the question needs
